Thanks for the updated order form. A few items from Legal/Procurement that we can’t accept as written in Exhibit A: the current rebate/chargeback trigger reads as a unilateral 'cap' that could be applied retroactively across tiers. We need: 1) a clear quarterly reconciliation runway (not a backdated clawback), 2) a predictable notice window for any pricing adjustments, and 3) an explicit migration credit if usage drops due to our internal product changes.

I attached our preferred markup (ACME_OrderForm_ExhibitA_redline.docx). High level: we prefer a reconciliation model rather than a retrospective cap. Proposed language excerpt: 

"Chargeback Corridor. Parties will perform a quarterly reconciliation (the 'Reconciliation') to true up actual usage against committed bands. Any adjustments resulting from Reconciliation will be applied prospectively to the following quarter, except where (i) material errors in metering are discovered, or (ii) fraud is established. Retroactive chargebacks that reduce previously invoiced credits are excluded.

Reconciliation Notice. Redwood shall provide at least 30 days' written notice before implementing any change to per-unit pricing or band thresholds that would affect billing in the upcoming quarter.

Migration Credit. If Customer reduces consumption due to a bona fide migration to an alternate internal system, Customer will be eligible for a migration credit equal to the unamortized portion of any prepaid committed credits, subject to verification and a documented migration plan."

Please let me know whether you can accept this shape or if your team needs different guardrails.

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear markup and the attachment. We're broadly aligned on keeping reconciliations predictable and avoiding retroactive surprises. Our concern is ensuring the mechanism doesn't allow large, unplanned revenue leakage in the event of short-term usage volatility (e.g., seasonality, one-off testing spikes).

Suggested compromise (operational summary):
- Keep a quarterly reconciliation cadence, but allow a single-statement prospective adjustment plus a limited retrospective correction window of one quarter for verified metering errors.
- Introduce a 'Reconciliation Cap' that limits retrospective adjustments to 10% of the quarter's billed amount (so we don't see outsized clawbacks).
- Preserve a 30-day notice for material pricing changes; for thresholds driven by model upgrades/quantization changes that materially alter per-token costs, allow a 60-day notice.
- Migration credit: agree in principle; request an explicit verification checklist and a two-quarter amortization schedule for any credits.

Draft language I propose we add to Exhibit A (below) — happy to have Marissa convert to legal redline: 

"Reconciliation and Chargeback. The Parties will reconcile actual usage against committed bands on a quarterly basis. Where a verified metering error is identified, Redwood may make an adjustment to prior invoices limited to amounts attributable to such error, not to exceed ten percent (10%) of the billed amount for the affected quarter. Except for verified errors, adjustments shall be applied prospectively.

Migration Credits. Should Customer materially reduce usage as part of a documented migration to an alternate system, Redwood will provide migration credits equal to the unamortized portion of any prepaid credits, amortized over two (2) subsequent quarters following Customer's submission of a migration plan and supporting evidence.

Notice. Redwood shall provide no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice for pricing or band threshold changes; for changes resulting from model architecture or quantization upgrades that meaningfully affect per-unit economics, Redwood shall provide sixty (60) days' prior notice."

I will loop in Marissa to turn this into a redline and explain the carveouts. If Acme agrees to the 10% retrospective cap and the two-quarter amortization for migration credits, I think we can move to execution quickly.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Samantha / all —

See attached: ACME_OrderForm_ExhibitA_v2.docx — we've incorporated Tessa's operational compromise and converted your markup into definitive legal text. Key legal points and rationale: 

1) Limited retrospective correction: We preserved your ask to avoid open-ended retroactive clawbacks but added a 10% cap on adjustments tied to verified metering errors. This protects both parties from meter/aggregation mistakes.
2) Prospectivity default: Absent verified error, adjustments go forward — preserves billing predictability.
3) Migration credit gate: To avoid opportunistic claims, migration credit requires (i) documented migration plan submitted 30 days before the end of the quarter and (ii) evidence demonstrating migration is the primary cause of reduced consumption. Credits amortize over two quarters to smooth financial impact.

Proposed redline excerpt (legal):

"Section 3.2 (Reconciliation). On a quarterly basis, Redwood and Customer shall reconcile actual usage to the applicable committed bands. If, and only if, either Party identifies a material metering error, the Parties shall correct prior invoices attributable to such error; provided, however, that any correction shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the billed amount for the quarter in which the error occurred. All other reconciliations shall be prospective.

Section 3.3 (Migration Credit). Customer may request a migration credit where reduction in Platform usage is the direct result of a documented migration. Customer must submit a migration plan and supporting evidence no later than thirty (30) days after the end of the quarter in which the reduction occurred. Migration credits, if granted, shall be amortized over two (2) subsequent quarters.

Section 3.4 (Notice). Redwood shall provide thirty (30) days prior written notice for pricing or band threshold changes; sixty (60) days for changes arising from model architecture or quantization modifications that materially affect per-unit pricing."

If Acme accepts these guardrails, we will apply the redline to the final order form and prepare DocuSign routing. If you want, I can add a short SLA note that reserves a one-time grace allowance for initial onboarding months.
